chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Amr ibn Uthman from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ibrahim Al-Karkhi who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'My wife died, may Allah have mercy on her, and she was compatible with me, and I intend to marry.' He said to me, 'Look where you place yourself, and who you share your wealth with and inform about your religion and your secret. If you are to do so, [choose] a virgin who is known for goodness and good character.'

And know that women are created in different types: some are a prize (gain), some are a burden (cost), and some are the crescent moon when it shines for its owner, and some are darkness. Whoever catches the good of them will be happy, and whoever catches the bad has no revenge (can only endure). And they are three types:

A virgin, fertile woman who helps her husband throughout his life for his worldly and afterlife affairs, and the world does not help against her; a barren woman who has no beauty and no character and does not help in goodness; and a noisy, restless, backbiting woman who considers much little and does not accept little.
ai.seo_question: What are the three types of women described in the hadith regarding marriage selection?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) guides a companion on remarriage by emphasizing the profound spiritual and domestic impact of a wife, who becomes a partner in wealth, faith, and secrets. He categorizes women into distinct archetypes, highlighting the ideal of a virgin, fertile wife who aids her husband in both worldly and religious affairs, while contrasting her with barren or difficult counterparts. This classification reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of linking marital compatibility to spiritual success (*sa'adah*) and practical household harmony.
